S03 plan. New src/solve/resume.ts: a run-state file next to history.jsonl in the git dir (.git/synthe/solve/<name>/run.json): run number, branch, base, scratch path, head commit of the kept state, rounds done, attempts (with before/after), baseline, calls, idle count, keptAny, status running|done. solve() writes it at start and after each finished round, and marks it done after result.json. --resume: if the state says running, prune the dead worktree, reopen the same branch at the saved head (or the base when nothing was kept), and continue at round done+1 with the saved attempts, calls and idle count; the baseline in result.json stays the first run's. A round that a kill cut short is not in the state, so it runs again; a finished round never does. If the state says done or is missing: say 'The last run ... ended normally. Starting a new run.' and run as usual. Small hooks: scratch.ts gets an optional reopen (h06: one optional argument), loop.ts runLoop gets optional start state (h05: optional fields only), cli/solve.ts gets --resume, types.ts SolveOptions gets resume?: boolean. Also: record() calls appendHistory without a run number, so each attempt counts as a new run; I pass the run number once.

S03 verdict: medium. The logic is small; the risk is the edge cases of a kill: a worktree left on disk, a commit made but its round not recorded, a branch deleted by the SIGTERM clean-up when nothing was kept. The state's head commit settles all three.

S03 PR #137: solve --resume. h05: loop.ts gets optional LoopOptions.resume and LoopSteps.roundDone; solve() writes .git/synthe/solve/<name>/run.json after each round; record() now passes one run number per run. h06: openScratch gets an optional 4th argument 'reopen'.
